text: First: March on the spot.
Next: March on the spot.
Lift the knees to hip height, swing the arms, breathe through the nose.
Easy pace. You should be able to talk.
Breathe through the nose.
First: Arm swings and shoulder rolls.
Next: Arm swings and shoulder rolls.
Swing both arms forward and back, then roll the shoulders backwards ten times.
First: Hip circles.
Next: Hip circles.
Hands on the hips, circle the pelvis slowly, five each way, then standing leg swings.
First: Cat-cow.
Next: Cat-cow.
On hands and knees, round and arch the spine with the breath, slowly through every segment.
First: Chin tuck.
Next: Chin tuck.
Sit or stand tall.
Slide the chin straight back as if making a double chin, keeping the eyes level.
Hold, then relax.
Focus on a lengthening at the back of the neck.
Let the base of your skull soften as you breathe out.
Avoid tipping the chin down.
Focus on the eyes stay level, the crown lifts.
A mild pull only. Never sharp.
Avoid clenching the jaw.
Let the back of your neck soften as you breathe out.
A quick twenty seconds to loosen up before the strength work.
First: Suboccipital release on tennis balls.
Next: Suboccipital release on tennis balls.
Lie on your back with two tennis balls in a sock under the base of the skull, knees bent.
Let the head rest and breathe slowly; nod the chin a few millimetres up and down.
Focus on letting the weight of the head sink onto the balls.
Avoid balls on the neck instead of the skull base.
Focus on slow breathing; the jaw unclenched.
Avoid pressing or rolling hard.
First: Upper trapezius stretch.
Next: Upper trapezius stretch.
Sit on one hand to hold that shoulder down.
Tilt the opposite ear toward the shoulder, then add light pressure with the other hand on the side of the head.
Focus on the pull along the top of the shoulder to the neck.
Let the top of your shoulder, up to your neck soften as you breathe out.
Avoid lifting the shoulder you are stretching.
Focus on the anchored shoulder stays down.
Avoid pulling the head with force.
First: Levator scapulae stretch.
Next: Levator scapulae stretch.
Reach one hand behind, as if holding a chair, to keep the shoulder blade down.
Turn the nose 45° toward the opposite armpit and let the head drop forward with light hand weight.
Focus on the pull at the upper inside corner of the shoulder blade.
Let the upper inside corner of your shoulder blade soften as you breathe out.
Avoid letting the shoulder shrug up.
Focus on the shoulder blade held down by the reaching hand.
Avoid pulling hard with the hand.
First: Sternocleidomastoid stretch.
Next: Sternocleidomastoid stretch.
Anchor one collarbone with the opposite hand.
Tilt the head away, then turn the chin slightly up and toward the anchored side.
Focus on the pull along the front and side of the neck.
Let the front and side of your neck soften as you breathe out.
Avoid holding longer than 20 seconds.
Focus on the collarbone anchored down.
Avoid dizziness or visual change: stop and skip it.
Let the side of your neck, above the collarbone soften as you breathe out.
First: Scalene stretch.
Next: Scalene stretch.
Hold the seat with one hand.
Tilt the head away and rotate the face slightly toward the stretching side, looking a little up.
Focus on breath into the belly during the hold.
Avoid lifting the chest with each breath.
Focus on a gentle pull from the side of the neck toward the collarbone.
Avoid any arm tingling.
First: Neck extensor stretch.
Next: Neck extensor stretch.
Tuck the chin, then let the head hang forward.
Clasp the hands behind the head and let their weight add to the stretch without pulling.
Focus on the chin tucked first, then the head hanging.
Avoid pulling with the hands.
Focus on hands only resting, not pulling.
Avoid rounding the whole upper back to cheat the stretch.
First: Jaw release.
Next: Jaw release.
Rest the tongue on the roof of the mouth, let the teeth part and the jaw hang.
Massage the masseter with slow circles for 30 seconds each side.
Focus on teeth apart, tongue resting on the palate.
Let the sides of your jaw soften as you breathe out.
Avoid opening wide or forcing the jaw.
Focus on slow circles on the masseter, the bulge when you clench.
Avoid pressing on a painful click.
First: Diaphragmatic breathing.
Next: Diaphragmatic breathing.
Lie with the knees bent, one hand on the chest and one on the belly.
Breathe in through the nose for four counts so only the lower hand rises, then out for six counts.
Focus on the lower hand rises first; the upper hand stays still.
Avoid big, forced breaths.
Focus on the exhale is longer than the inhale.
Avoid lifting the shoulders with the inhale.
Let just below your collarbone, near the shoulder soften as you breathe out.
First: Doorway chest stretch, elbows low.
Next: Doorway chest stretch, elbows low.
Forearms on a door frame with the elbows below shoulder height.
Step one foot through until a stretch runs across the upper chest.
Focus on a stretch across the upper chest, not the shoulder joint.
Let the front of your chest soften as you breathe out.
Avoid arching the lower back.
Focus on ribs down, chin tucked.
Avoid letting the shoulder blades roll forward.
Let the front and side of your shoulder soften as you breathe out.
Let the inner front of your upper arm soften as you breathe out.
First: Doorway chest stretch, elbows high.
Next: Doorway chest stretch, elbows high.
Forearms on the frame with the elbows above shoulder height.
Lean through until the stretch is felt lower on the chest and near the front of the shoulder.
Focus on the stretch lower on the chest and under the collarbone.
Avoid elbows so high the shoulder pinches.
Focus on the shoulder blades pulled gently back.
Avoid leaning with the head forward.
Let the deep front of your shoulder soften as you breathe out.
First: Single-arm wall chest stretch.
Next: Single-arm wall chest stretch.
Palm and forearm on a wall at shoulder height, elbow bent 90°.
Turn the body slowly away from the wall.
Focus on the chest opening, the shoulder blade staying back.
Avoid letting the shoulder roll forward toward the wall.
Focus on turning from the feet and hips.
Avoid a stretch felt inside the shoulder joint.
First: Hands clasped behind the back.
Next: Hands clasped behind the back.
Clasp the hands behind the back, straighten the elbows and lift the hands slightly while the chest opens.
Focus on lifting from the shoulders, the chest opening.
Avoid arching the lower back to lift the hands.
Focus on standing tall through the crown.
Avoid letting the head poke forward.
Let the front of your upper arm soften as you breathe out.
First: Cross-body shoulder stretch.
Next: Cross-body shoulder stretch.
Bring one arm across the chest at shoulder height and hold it above the elbow with the other hand, drawing it gently closer.
Focus on the pull in the back of the shoulder.
Let the back of your shoulder soften as you breathe out.
Avoid lifting the shoulder.
Focus on the shoulder down away from the ear.
Avoid rotating the trunk toward the arm.
Let the back of your shoulder blade soften as you breathe out.
Let the back of your armpit soften as you breathe out.
First: Sleeper stretch.
Next: Sleeper stretch.
Lie on one side with that shoulder blade pinned, upper arm forward and elbow bent 90°.
Use the top hand to press the forearm gently toward the floor.
Focus on the shoulder blade pinned against the floor.
Avoid pressing into pinching pain at the front.
Focus on a mild pull in the back of the shoulder.
Avoid lifting the shoulder blade off the floor.
First: Doorway external rotation stretch.
Next: Doorway external rotation stretch.
Elbow at the side bent 90°, back of the forearm against a door frame.
Turn the body away so the forearm rotates outward.
Focus on the elbow glued to the ribs.
Avoid letting the elbow drift away from the body.
Focus on the forearm rotating outward.
Avoid rotating the trunk instead of the arm.
First: Wall lat stretch.
Next: Wall lat stretch.
Hands on a wall at hip height, walk the feet back and hinge at the hips until the trunk is level, letting the chest sink between the arms.
Focus on the chest sinking between the arms.
Let the side of your back, below the armpit soften as you breathe out.
Avoid rounding or arching the lower back.
Focus on the pull in the sides of the back and the armpits.
Avoid shrugging the shoulders to the ears.
Let the back of your upper arm soften as you breathe out.
First: Child pose with side reach.
Next: Child pose with side reach.
From kneeling, sit back toward the heels and walk both hands to one side along the floor.
Focus on hips back toward the heels.
Avoid letting the hips lift forward.
Focus on the far side of the back lengthening.
Avoid collapsing the chest.
Let the long muscles beside your spine soften as you breathe out.
Let the side of your lower back, between ribs and hip soften as you breathe out.
First: Overhead triceps stretch.
Next: Overhead triceps stretch.
Reach one hand down the back with the elbow pointing up.
Use the other hand to pull the elbow gently behind the head.
Focus on the elbow pointing to the ceiling.
Avoid arching the back to get further.
Focus on ribs down, neck long.
Avoid pushing the head forward with the arm.
First: Wall biceps stretch.
Next: Wall biceps stretch.
Palm flat on a wall behind you at shoulder height, fingers back, arm straight.
Turn the body away slowly.
Focus on a stretch along the front of the arm.
Avoid any tingling in the hand.
Focus on shoulder blade back and down.
Avoid letting the shoulder roll forward.
Let the front of your elbow soften as you breathe out.
Let the inside of your forearm soften as you breathe out.
First: Thread the needle.
Next: Thread the needle.
On hands and knees, slide one arm under the body, palm up, until the shoulder and ear rest on the floor.
Breathe, then reverse and open the arm toward the ceiling.
Focus on the twist coming from the upper back.
Let the space between your shoulder blades soften as you breathe out.
Avoid collapsing onto the neck.
Focus on hips staying over the knees.
Avoid moving the hips to fake the twist.
First: Self-hug upper-back stretch.
Next: Self-hug upper-back stretch.
Wrap the arms around yourself, grab the shoulder blades and round the upper back while breathing into the back of the ribs.
Focus on the shoulder blades sliding apart.
Avoid dropping the head.
Focus on breath into the back of the ribs.
Avoid hunching the shoulders up.
First: Thoracic extension over a foam roll.
Next: Thoracic extension over a foam roll.
Lie with a foam roll across the mid-back, hands behind the head.
On each out-breath extend gently over the roll, then sit up a little.
Move the roll one segment and repeat.
Focus on extension over the roll on the out-breath.
Avoid the roll below the bottom ribs.
Focus on hands supporting the head.
Avoid dropping the head back unsupported.
Let the front of your belly soften as you breathe out.
Let the side of your ribs, under the armpit soften as you breathe out.
First: Open book rotation.
Next: Open book rotation.
Lie on one side with the knees bent and arms together in front.
Open the top arm toward the other side, following it with the eyes, and let the chest turn.
Focus on the knees staying together on the floor.
Avoid letting the top knee lift.
Focus on the eyes following the hand.
Avoid forcing the shoulder to the floor.
Let the side of your waist soften as you breathe out.
Let the small deep muscles along your lower spine soften as you breathe out.
First: Pendulum swings.
Next: Pendulum swings.
Lean on a table with the free arm hanging.
Let the body sway so the arm swings in small circles and lines without muscular effort.
Focus on the arm completely passive.
Let the top of your shoulder blade soften as you breathe out.
Avoid using the shoulder muscles to swing.
Focus on movement coming from the body swaying.
Avoid large circles too soon.
First: Arm circles.
Next: Arm circles.
Arms out to the sides, draw slow circles that grow from small to the largest pain-free size, forward then backward.
Focus on small circles growing slowly.
Avoid shrugging as the arms go up.
Focus on shoulders down, breath easy.
Avoid fast or forced circles.
First: Wrist flexor stretch.
Next: Wrist flexor stretch.
Arm straight in front, palm up.
With the other hand draw the fingers back toward the body.
Focus on the elbow straight.
Avoid bending the elbow to reduce it.
Focus on the pull along the inside of the forearm to the elbow.
Avoid pulling single fingers.
First: Wrist extensor stretch.
Next: Wrist extensor stretch.
Arm straight in front, palm down.
With the other hand press the back of the hand so the wrist bends down, fingers curled.
Focus on the elbow straight, fingers curled.
Let the outside of your forearm soften as you breathe out.
Avoid letting the shoulder shrug.
Focus on the pull on the outside of the forearm.
Avoid forcing the wrist.
First: Sphinx and cobra.
Next: Sphinx and cobra.
Lie face down, prop on the forearms or hands, and let the front of the body lengthen while the hips stay on the floor.
Focus on the front of the body lengthening from the hips.
Avoid pinching in the lower back: lower down.
Focus on buttocks relaxed, breathing into the belly.
Avoid shrugging into the ears.
Let the deep front of your hip soften as you breathe out.
Let the front of your hip soften as you breathe out.
First: Standing side bend.
Next: Standing side bend.
Feet hip width, reach one arm overhead and lean away from it, pushing the hip out to the same side.
Focus on leaning in one flat plane, like between two walls.
Avoid twisting or leaning forward.
Focus on the hip pushed out to the opposite side.
Avoid collapsing the ribs on the short side.
First: Seated quadratus lumborum stretch.
Next: Seated quadratus lumborum stretch.
Sit with the feet flat, hold the chair with one hand and reach the other arm up and over to the opposite side, lifting the ribs away from the hip.
Focus on both sitting bones staying down.
Avoid lifting one buttock.
Focus on ribs lifting away from the hip.
Avoid dropping the arm forward.
On hands and knees, round the whole spine toward the ceiling on the out-breath, then let it sag and lift the chest on the in-breath.
Focus on every segment of the spine moving.
Avoid moving only the lower back.
Focus on the breath leading the movement.
Avoid fast rocking.
First: Knees to chest.
Next: Knees to chest.
On your back, hug both knees toward the chest and let the lower back round into the floor.
Focus on the lower back rounding into the floor.
Avoid pulling the knees hard with knee pain.
Focus on hands behind the thighs, not on the knees.
Avoid lifting the head.
Let your buttock soften as you breathe out.
First: Supine twist.
Next: Supine twist.
On your back, knees bent, arms out.
Let the knees fall to one side while the opposite shoulder stays down.
Focus on the opposite shoulder staying down.
Avoid forcing the knees to the floor.
Focus on letting the knees fall by their own weight.
Avoid twisting from the neck.
Let the outer side of your hip soften as you breathe out.
First: Seated spinal twist.
Next: Seated spinal twist.
Sit tall, cross the arms or hold the chair back, and turn the chest to one side from the mid-back, eyes following.
Focus on growing tall first, then turning.
Avoid pulling hard on the chair.
Focus on the turn from the mid-back, hips facing forward.
Avoid twisting from the neck only.
First: Prayer stretch.
Next: Prayer stretch.
From kneeling, sit the hips back toward the heels and reach both arms forward along the floor, chest sinking.
Avoid hips lifting forward.
Focus on the chest sinking, the armpits lengthening.
Avoid shoulders shrugging.
First: Half-kneeling hip flexor stretch.
Next: Half-kneeling hip flexor stretch.
Back knee on a cushion, front foot forward.
Tuck the tailbone under, squeeze the back-side buttock and shift forward until the front of the hip stretches.
Focus on the tailbone tucked under before shifting forward.
Avoid arching the lower back.
Focus on the buttock of the kneeling side squeezed.
Avoid leaning the trunk forward.
Let the front of your thigh, up to the hip soften as you breathe out.
Let the outer front of your hip soften as you breathe out.
First: Half-kneeling psoas stretch with reach.
Next: Half-kneeling psoas stretch with reach.
In the half-kneeling position, raise the arm on the kneeling side and side-bend slightly away from it.
Focus on the reach adding length to the side of the trunk.
Avoid side-bending so far the pelvis untucks.
Focus on tailbone still tucked.
Avoid shrugging the raised arm.
First: Thomas-position hip flexor stretch.
Next: Thomas-position hip flexor stretch.
Lie at the edge of a bed, hug one knee to the chest and let the other leg hang off the edge, relaxed.
Focus on the hanging thigh fully relaxed.
Avoid lifting the hanging leg with its own muscles.
Focus on the lower back flat with the held knee.
Avoid letting the back arch as the knee is released.
Let the front of your hip and inner knee soften as you breathe out.
First: Couch stretch.
Next: Couch stretch.
Kneel with one shin up against a wall or sofa, the other foot forward.
Tuck the tailbone and lift the trunk upright.
Focus on tailbone tucked, trunk lifting upright over weeks.
Avoid arching the back to get upright.
Focus on the stretch down the front of the thigh and hip.
Avoid knee pain: pad the knee or back off.
Let the front of your thigh soften as you breathe out.
Let the outer front of your thigh soften as you breathe out.
First: Standing quadriceps stretch.
Next: Standing quadriceps stretch.
Hold a wall.
Bring one heel toward the buttock, knees together, pelvis tucked, hips pushed forward.
Focus on knees together, pelvis tucked.
Avoid pulling the knee out to the side.
Focus on hips pushed forward slightly.
Avoid arching the back.
Let the inner front of your thigh, above the knee soften as you breathe out.
First: Figure-4 stretch.
Next: Figure-4 stretch.
On your back, cross one ankle over the opposite knee and pull that thigh toward the chest.
Focus on the pull deep in the buttock.
Avoid lifting the head and shoulders.
Focus on the crossed ankle flexed to protect the knee.
Avoid pressure on the crossed knee.
Let deep in your buttock soften as you breathe out.
First: Seated figure-4 stretch.
Next: Seated figure-4 stretch.
Sitting, place one ankle on the opposite knee and hinge forward from the hips with a long spine.
Focus on hinging forward with a long spine.
Avoid rounding the back to get lower.
Focus on the pull in the buttock of the crossed leg.
Avoid pushing down on the crossed knee.
First: Pigeon pose.
Next: Pigeon pose.
From hands and knees, bring one knee forward behind the wrist, shin across, and slide the other leg straight back.
Lower the trunk over the front leg.
Focus on the pelvis level.
Avoid twisting the front knee.
Focus on breathing into the outer hip.
Avoid collapsing the hips to one side.
First: Knee to opposite shoulder.
Next: Knee to opposite shoulder.
On your back, pull one knee across the body toward the opposite shoulder.
Focus on the pull in the outer buttock.
Avoid lifting the opposite shoulder.
Focus on the other leg long on the floor.
Avoid pulling the knee straight to the chest.
First: 90/90 hip stretch.
Next: 90/90 hip stretch.
Sit with the front shin across in front of you and the back shin pointing behind, both knees at 90°.
Sit tall and lean the chest over the front shin, then over the back thigh.
Focus on sitting tall on the sitting bones.
Avoid rounding the back to lean.
Focus on leaning from the hips over each thigh.
Avoid letting the pelvis tip back.
Let your inner thigh soften as you breathe out.
First: Standing cross-over hip stretch.
Next: Standing cross-over hip stretch.
Cross one leg behind the other, push the hip of the back leg out sideways and reach the same-side arm overhead.
Focus on the hip pushed out, the arm reaching over.
Avoid leaning forward.
Focus on the pull on the outer hip of the back leg.
Avoid locking the knees.
First: Butterfly stretch.
Next: Butterfly stretch.
Sit with the soles together, hold the feet, sit tall and let the knees drop; hinge forward from the hips.
Focus on sitting tall, hinging from the hips.
Let your inner thigh, near the groin soften as you breathe out.
Avoid pushing the knees down with the hands or elbows.
Focus on the knees dropping by their weight.
Avoid rounding the lower back.
Let the long line of your inner thigh soften as you breathe out.
First: Frog stretch.
Next: Frog stretch.
On hands and knees, widen the knees with the feet turned out, then rock the hips back toward the heels.
Focus on rocking back slowly toward the heels.
Avoid letting the back arch.
Focus on the lower back flat.
Avoid knee pain: pad or reduce the width.
First: Side lunge adductor stretch.
Next: Side lunge adductor stretch.
Wide stance, bend one knee and sit toward that side, keeping the other leg straight with the foot flat.
Focus on the bent knee tracking over the foot.
Avoid the bent knee collapsing inward.
Focus on the straight leg foot flat, toes forward.
Avoid rounding the trunk forward.
Let the back of your thigh, inner side soften as you breathe out.
First: Deep squat hold.
Next: Deep squat hold.
Feet slightly wider than the hips, sink into a full squat and hold the knees apart with the elbows, chest up.
Focus on heels down, chest up.
Avoid heels lifting.
Focus on elbows gently pressing the knees apart.
Avoid rounding the lower back hard.
Let the lower part of your calf, toward the heel soften as you breathe out.
First: Supine hamstring stretch with strap.
Next: Supine hamstring stretch with strap.
On your back, loop a strap round one foot, straighten the knee and raise the leg to a mild pull behind the thigh.
Focus on the knee straight, the pull behind the thigh.
Let the back of your thigh, outer side soften as you breathe out.
Avoid pulling the leg with the knee bent.
Focus on the other leg flat on the floor.
Avoid lifting the hip or head.
Let the upper part of your calf soften as you breathe out.
First: Standing hamstring stretch, heel on a step.
Next: Standing hamstring stretch, heel on a step.
Heel on a low step, knee straight, hinge forward from the hips with the back flat and chest toward the thigh.
Focus on hinging from the hips with a flat back.
Avoid rounding the back to reach lower.
Focus on chest toward the thigh.
Avoid locking the knee hard.
Let the back of your knee soften as you breathe out.
First: Seated hamstring stretch.
Next: Seated hamstring stretch.
Sit with one leg straight and the other bent.
Hinge forward over the straight leg with a long spine.
Focus on a long spine, hinging from the hips.
Avoid rounding the back and reaching with the hands.
Focus on chest reaching toward the foot.
Avoid bouncing.
First: World's greatest stretch.
Next: World's greatest stretch.
Long lunge, both hands inside the front foot.
Drop the inside elbow toward the floor, then rotate that arm to the ceiling, then rock back and straighten the front knee.
Focus on a long lunge with the back leg straight.
Avoid rushing the positions.
Focus on the chest opening as the arm rotates up.
Avoid letting the front knee collapse inward.
First: Leg swings.
Next: Leg swings.
Hold a wall and swing one straight leg forward and back, growing the range with each swing.
Focus on swinging from the hip, trunk tall.
Avoid arching the back as the leg swings back.
Focus on range growing gradually.
Avoid swinging from the lower back.
First: Wall calf stretch, knee straight.
Next: Wall calf stretch, knee straight.
Hands on a wall, back leg straight with the heel down and toes forward.
Lean in until the calf stretches.
Focus on heel down, toes pointing straight forward.
Avoid the foot rolling inward.
Focus on the arch lifted.
Avoid bending the back knee.
Let the sole of your foot soften as you breathe out.
First: Wall calf stretch, knee bent.
Next: Wall calf stretch, knee bent.
Same position with the back knee slightly bent and the heel down; sink the knee forward.
Focus on the stretch lower, near the Achilles.
Avoid the heel lifting.
Focus on heel down, knee sinking forward.
Avoid the knee collapsing inward.
Let the inside of your lower leg and arch soften as you breathe out.
Let the sole of your foot and deep calf soften as you breathe out.
First: Stair heel drop.
Next: Stair heel drop.
Balls of the feet on a step, hold the rail, let one heel sink below the step.
Focus on letting the heel sink slowly.
Focus on holding the rail for balance.
Avoid dropping fast.
First: Knee-to-wall ankle mobility.
Next: Knee-to-wall ankle mobility.
Foot a hand's width from a wall, drive the knee forward over the toes to touch the wall without the heel lifting.
Move the foot back as it gets easier.
Focus on the knee driving straight over the toes.
Avoid the heel lifting.
Focus on the heel staying down.
Avoid the knee drifting inward.
First: Kneeling shin stretch.
Next: Kneeling shin stretch.
Kneel and sit back on the heels with the tops of the feet flat on the floor; lean back slightly.
Focus on tops of the feet flat.
Let the front of your shin soften as you breathe out.
Avoid knee pain: skip.
Focus on leaning back slowly.
Avoid sitting back hard too quickly.
Let the front of your ankle and top of your foot soften as you breathe out.
First: Toe extension plantar fascia stretch.
Next: Toe extension plantar fascia stretch.
Toes up against a wall with the heel on the floor, lean the knee toward the wall.
Focus on toes up the wall, heel on the floor.
Avoid bending the knee a lot.
Focus on the pull along the sole.
Avoid pressing the toes painfully.
First: Peroneal stretch.
Next: Peroneal stretch.
Sitting with the ankle on the opposite knee, hold the forefoot and turn the sole upward and inward.
Focus on the sole turning upward and inward.
Let the outside of your lower leg soften as you breathe out.
Avoid twisting the knee.
Focus on the pull along the outside of the lower leg.
Avoid forcing the ankle.
First: Downward dog.
Next: Downward dog.
Hands and feet on the floor, hips lifted high.
Press the chest toward the thighs and pedal the heels toward the floor.
Focus on hips high, spine long.
Avoid rounding the back.
Focus on heels pedalling toward the floor.
Avoid shoulders shrugged into the ears.
First: Supine chin tuck holds.
Next: Supine chin tuck holds.
Lie on your back, knees bent.
Nod the chin gently as if saying "yes" so the back of the neck lengthens; hold without lifting the head.
Focus on a small nod, the back of the neck lengthening.
Feel the deep front of your neck doing the work.
Focus on the deep front-of-neck muscles, not the surface ones.
Breathe out on the effort.
Avoid the surface neck muscles bulging.
First: Chin tuck and lift.
Next: Chin tuck and lift.
From the chin tuck, lift the head one to two centimetres off the floor and hold, keeping the chin tucked.
Focus on the chin tucked throughout the lift.
Avoid poking the chin.
Focus on a lift of one to two centimetres only.
Avoid lifting high.
Feel the front and side of your neck doing the work.
First: Isometric neck in four directions.
Next: Isometric neck in four directions.
Press the head gently into your hand placed on the forehead, then the back of the head, then each side, without any movement.
Focus on about 30% effort.
Feel the back of your neck doing the work.
Avoid pushing hard.
Focus on no movement at all.
Avoid holding the breath.
Feel the side of your neck, above the collarbone doing the work.
Feel the top of your shoulder, up to your neck doing the work.
First: Prone neck extension holds.
Next: Prone neck extension holds.
Lie face down with the forehead on the hands.
Tuck the chin and lift the head a few centimetres, keeping the eyes on the floor.
Focus on a long neck, eyes on the floor.
Avoid looking up.
Focus on the chin tucked as the head lifts.
Feel the base of your skull doing the work.
First: Band row.
Next: Band row.
Band anchored at chest height.
Pull the elbows back past the ribs, squeezing the shoulder blades together and down.
Focus on elbows back past the ribs, shoulder blades together and down.
Feel the space between your shoulder blades doing the work.
Avoid shrugging toward the ears.
Focus on the chest open at the end.
Avoid leaning back to pull.
Feel the back of your shoulder doing the work.
Feel the front of your upper arm doing the work.
First: Face pull.
Next: Face pull.
Band at face height.
Pull toward the face with the elbows high, finishing with the hands beside the ears and the forearms vertical.
Focus on elbows high, hands finishing beside the ears.
Avoid pulling to the chest instead of the face.
Focus on the forearms rotating up at the end.
Avoid shrugging.
Feel the back of your shoulder blade doing the work.
Feel the lower tips of your shoulder blades doing the work.
First: Prone T raise.
Next: Prone T raise.
Face down, arms out to the sides with thumbs up.
Lift the arms by squeezing the shoulder blades together.
Focus on the shoulder blades squeezing together.
Focus on thumbs up, neck long.
Avoid lifting with the lower back.
First: Prone Y raise.
Next: Prone Y raise.
Face down, arms overhead in a Y with thumbs up.
Lift the arms by drawing the shoulder blades down and in.
Focus on shoulder blades drawn down and in.
Avoid shrugging the shoulders up.
Focus on thumbs up.
Feel the side of your ribs, under the armpit doing the work.
Feel the front and side of your shoulder doing the work.
First: Prone W external rotation.
Next: Prone W external rotation.
Face down, elbows bent and out to the side.
Rotate the forearms up toward the ceiling while squeezing the shoulder blades.
Focus on forearms rotating up, elbows at shoulder height.
Avoid elbows dropping below the shoulders.
Focus on the shoulder blades squeezing.
Avoid lifting the chest.
First: Band external rotation.
Next: Band external rotation.
